= Repeated Glasgow Marriages, 1400–Present =

<small>'''Glasgow Name Study:''' [[Space:Glasgow Name Study|project home]] · [[Space:Glasgow Research|research directory]] · [[Space:Glasgow Kinship Circle|kinship circle]] · [https://glasgow.phenotype.dev/compare compare people]</small>


This is the central marriage-association page. [[Space:Glasgow Unions|Glasgow Unions]] provides a shorter route into the same research, while the detailed marriage lists and interpretation are presented here.

This page is part of the '''Glasgow One-Name Study'''. It analyses two profile-sets drawn from the project’s working spreadsheets (''File 1'' = 1400-1800; ''File 2'' = 1400-Present) to show which spouse surnames recur. The counts describe the profile dataset; they do not establish that people sharing a spouse surname were related, belonged to one social circle, or participated in a coordinated migration or property network.

* ''File 1'' – 809 profiles, 41 repeat pairings (up to 1800)
* ''File 2'' – 3 545 profiles, 1 201 repeat pairings (1400-present)

Records where '''LNAB = Current''' or either surname was ''Unknown'' were excluded. Spelling variants (e.g. ''Nicol'' ≈ ''Nichol'') were merged when their Levenshtein similarity was ≥ 0.85.

== Top 10 Families (1400-1800): Backgrounds and Marriages ==
The summaries below explain who these families were and list the specific Glasgow marriages involving them recorded between 1400 and 1800. Birth years are shown where known.

=== Cunningham (6 Marriages) ===
Six profiles in the pre-1800 dataset have a Cunningham spouse. Each marriage must be evaluated separately: the shared surname does not prove descent from the Earls of Glencairn, connection to an Ulster undertaker, or access to land.
* [[Cunningham-20923|Jonet Cunningham (b. 1580)]] ⇒ married '''[[Glasgow-1027|Robert Glasgow (abt.1583-aft.1647)]]'''
* [[Cunningham-20924|Jean Cunningham (b. 1660)]] ⇒ married '''[[Glasgow-1073|John Glasgow M.A (abt.1653-abt.1721)]]''' was said to be ''"daughter of John Cuninghame of Wattieston, Chamberlain to the Laird of Glengarnock, of the family of Robert-land"''
* [[Cunningham-20925|Janet Cunningham (b. 1719)]] ⇒ married '''[[Glasgow-1227|Abraham Glasgow (1719-)]]''' in Livingston. 
* [[Cunningham-20926|Agnes Cunningham (b. 1755)]] ⇒ married '''[[Glasgow-1321|Alexander Glasgow (bef.1747-)]]''' in Kirknewton
* [[Glasgow-543|Nancy Glasgow (b. 1786)]] ⇐ married '''[[Cunningham-13540|Abraham Cunningham (1786-1861)]]'''
* [[Cunningham-20927|Jean Cunningham (b. 1798)]] ⇒ married '''[[Glasgow-1483|James Glasgow (abt.1790-abt.1833)]]''' in Govan.

== What the pattern establishes ==
{| cellpadding="6" style="border:1px solid #aaa; background:#f9f9f9"
|-
| '''Observed''' || Some spouse surnames recur in the working profile datasets. The linked profiles provide a practical queue for checking marriage records and distinguishing same-named families.
|-
| '''Not established''' || The counts do not prove that spouses with the same surname were related, that marriages were strategic, or that the couples shared property, trade, political, religious or migration networks.
|-
| '''Next step''' || Verify each marriage against an original register or dependable transcript, identify both sets of parents where possible, and only then test whether two couples belong to the same documented kin group.
|}

== Modern-Period Leader Families (brief profiles) ==

'''1400-Present: ten current leaders'''

* '''Henry''' – Ulster sept Ó hInneirghe plus Lowland Hendrys; supplied kirk elders and schoolmasters across Ulster and the Ohio Valley.
* '''Bell''' – Border riding clan pacified by relocation to Ulster; later pillars of frontier Presbyterian communities in America.
* '''Patton''' – Border variant of Patrick; Colonel James Patton’s Shenandoah settlement illustrates the family’s pioneer drive.
* '''Campbell''' – Argyll magnates whose cadets flooded Glasgow; by 1841 Campbell was the city’s commonest surname, giving the Glasgow clan cousins in every municipal office.
